summary: Resilient static routing is configured and persistent. Direct primary-transit is preferred; failover through VyOS completed in ~2.01 seconds and direct-path restoration in ~1.01 seconds. Source addresses and management-plane isolation were preserved. All three nodes passed sequential reboot verification.
actions_performed: Configured persistent endpoint addressing, metric-10 direct routes, and metric-100 VyOS fallback routes.
Enabled one-second direct-path health monitoring on both Ubuntu endpoints.
Configured and saved VyOS forwarding exclusively between lan-a and lan-b, without NAT.
Tested failover, recovery, source preservation, and final bidirectional connectivity.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Preferred direct routing and final health
evidence.summary: Both endpoints have active services, both static routes, metric-10 primary selection, isolated management routes, and successful bidirectional probes.
Direct-link disruption converged through node1 in 2009 ms with working bidirectional routing.
The preferred route returned in 1019 ms and traffic resumed over primary-transit.
Captures prove 10.10.10.2 remained unchanged on the direct path and across both VyOS forwarding interfaces.

evidence.requirement: Management network excluded from routed data plane
evidence.summary: Data routes use only enp8s0/enp9s0 and eth1/eth2; management remains on enp1s0/eth0. VyOS permits only lan-a↔lan-b forwarding and has no NAT configuration.
After every node rebooted, failover again completed in 2010 ms through node1 and direct routing returned in 1014 ms.
Healthy baseline captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed, and VyOS service, interfaces, routes, peers, and firewall recovered.
